method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines' (published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21)), 27 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC9780550). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549) 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults' (published 14 June 2021), 9 claims; LICENCE: © 2021 Infectious Diseases Society of America. All rights reserved (no open licence) (read at the guideline's Notes section and page footer on idsociety.org). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Chosen over ESCMID 2021 (CC BY-NC-ND, publisher page returned a bot challenge, HTTP 403, not bypassed) and the ASID 2025 update (closed access). WSES 2019 (CC BY) was readable but predates the 2021 IDSA/SHEA and ESCMID changes. Edition 2.0 adds the IDSA/SHEA 2021 focused update itself (S2), read in full from the IDSA website (the OUP journal page returned a bot challenge, not bypassed); it covers only fidaxomicin and bezlotoxumab. Its page carries this clause, recorded verbatim: 'No part of this publication may be reproduced, stored in a retrieval system, transmitted, used for text and data mining, or used for training artificial intelligence, in any form or by any means, without the prior permission in writing, or as expressly permitted by law, by license or under terms agreed with the appropriate reprographics rights organization.' Per the owner's standing decision it is paraphrased and hash-anchored, not quoted. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Table 2 (treatment regimens and doses in the IDSA/SHEA 2021, ESCMID 2021 and ASID 2016 guidelines) added; S1 Table 1 (severity definitions) has ragged rows and was not extracted. S2 was read from a web page and has no appended tables.

claims.claim: **Non-severe CDI (IDSA/SHEA):** white cell count at or below 15 000 cells/mL and creatinine under 1.5 mg/dL. ESCMID adds temperature at or below 38.5°C, a creatinine rise of no more than 50% above baseline and no imaging signs of severity.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe CDI:** white cell count over 15 000 cells/mL or creatinine of 1.5 mg/dL or more (IDSA/SHEA). ESCMID also counts fever over 38.5°C or imaging showing colonic distension, pericolonic fat stranding or wall thickening.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fulminant (severe-complicated) CDI** means hypotension or shock, ileus or toxic megacolon; ESCMID adds raised lactate, perforation or any fulminant course.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refractory CDI** is disease not responding to recommended antibiotics, that is, no response after 3–5 days.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IDSA/SHEA and ESCMID now prefer fidaxomicin for a first episode**; vancomycin is acceptable, and metronidazole only when neither is available.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recurrence follows 20%–30% of courses of metronidazole or vancomycin**, and after one recurrence the chance of another is 50%–60%. Fidaxomicin is better at preventing recurrence.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vancomycin beat metronidazole** in two placebo-controlled trials; a Cochrane analysis of 22 trials, mostly non-severe disease, gave moderate-quality evidence that vancomycin is superior in all cases.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severity changes over time**, so reserving metronidazole for 'non-severe' cases risks under-treatment: one study found CDI-attributable 90-day mortality of 21.7% when under-treated against 8.9% when appropriately treated.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The IDSA/SHEA guideline grades its preference for fidaxomicin in a first episode as conditional, on moderate-certainty evidence;** it values fidaxomicin's benefit and safety, notes that uptake depends on resources, and keeps vancomycin as an acceptable alternative.
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pooling 4 trials, fidaxomicin gave more sustained responses 4 weeks after the end of treatment than vancomycin (risk ratio 1.16) and the same rate of initial cure (risk ratio 1.00).**
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The regimens compared for a first episode were oral fidaxomicin 200 mg 2 times a day and oral vancomycin 125 mg 4 times a day.**
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Risk factors for recurrence include age 65 or over, weakened immunity, severe disease and infection with ribotype 027/078/244 strains;** whether fidaxomicin adds more benefit in these groups has not been tested in prospective trials.
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First non-severe episode, regimens compared (S1 Table 2):** IDSA/SHEA 2021 and ESCMID 2021 prefer standard fidaxomicin (200 mg by mouth every 12 hours for 10 days), with oral vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours for 10 days as the alternative; if neither is available, oral metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours for 10–14 days (IDSA/SHEA) or 10 days (ESCMID). ESCMID adds extended-pulsed fidaxomicin, or bezlotoxumab when fidaxomicin is unavailable, for those at high recurrence risk, especially older inpatients. The older ASID 2016 advice was metronidazole 400 mg every 8 hours for 10 days.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fidaxomicin's main barrier to wider use is its high cost.**
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Oral metronidazole is not appropriate for severe CDI**; all guidelines agree.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The older ASID guideline advises oral vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours for 10 days in severe disease** and does not recommend fidaxomicin; ESCMID and IDSA/SHEA accept fidaxomicin as non-inferior. There are no data for fidaxomicin in life-threatening disease.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe CDI regimens compared (S1 Table 2):** IDSA/SHEA 2021 and ESCMID 2021: standard fidaxomicin or oral vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours for 10 days; IDSA/SHEA adds bezlotoxumab for a first episode with other recurrence risk factors (age 65 or over, immunocompromise) or an episode in the previous 6 months. ASID 2016: vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours for 10 days, and if oral therapy cannot be taken, vancomycin by nasogastric tube plus IV metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours, with or without rectal vancomycin.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **IDSA/SHEA 2021 for fulminant CDI:** no fidaxomicin; add IV metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours to higher-dose vancomycin 500 mg every 6 hours by mouth or nasogastric tube, with rectal vancomycin retention enemas every 6 hours if there is ileus. ESCMID instead allows fidaxomicin, does not routinely add IV metronidazole and suggests adding IV tigecycline.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fulminant CDI regimens compared (S1 Table 2):** IDSA/SHEA: vancomycin 500 mg every 6 hours by mouth or nasogastric tube plus IV metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours, and consider rectal vancomycin if there is ileus. ESCMID: standard fidaxomicin or oral vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours for 10 days, considering IV tigecycline (100 mg loading dose, then 50 mg every 12 hours), with a surgical opinion. ASID 2016: vancomycin up to 500 mg every 6 hours by mouth or nasogastric tube, with or without rectal vancomycin, plus IV metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours, and a surgical opinion. Rectal vancomycin is a retention enema of 500 mg in 100 mL of saline every 6 hours.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refractory fulminant CDI (S1 Table 2):** the IDSA/SHEA focused update is silent; ESCMID: surgery, or rescue FMT if surgery is not possible; ASID 2016: consider tigecycline alone or rescue FMT, and consider surgery.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Get a surgical referral alongside medical treatment** in deteriorating patients, but avoid total colectomy where possible, particularly without toxic megacolon; ESCMID suggests partial colectomy or loop ileostomy may spare total colectomy.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tigecycline can cause liver derangement, coagulopathy or pancreatitis**; monitor closely, stop early if adverse effects appear, and note courses over 14 days raise the coagulopathy risk.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rescue faecal microbiota transplant (FMT)** for refractory disease: ESCMID supports considering it when surgery is not feasible, and Australasian guidelines when medical therapy fails; IDSA/SHEA has not endorsed it here.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bezlotoxumab** (a single infusion of anti-toxin B antibody) lowers recurrence. Both IDSA/SHEA and ESCMID support it for a second episode within 6 months; in heart failure reserve it for when benefit outweighs risk, as more deaths occurred (19.5% vs 12.5%). It is not yet endorsed in Australian guidelines.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For any recurrence, IDSA/SHEA suggests fidaxomicin, standard or extended-pulsed, over a standard vancomycin course (conditional, low certainty).** After a first recurrence a standard or tapered-and-pulsed vancomycin course is acceptable; after several recurrences the choices are tapered-and-pulsed vancomycin, vancomycin followed by rifaximin, faecal microbiota transplant, or fidaxomicin.
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Extended-pulsed fidaxomicin (EXTEND trial) had among the lowest recurrence rates ever reported, 2% against 17% with vancomycin at day 40,** but it was compared with a standard vancomycin course, and its initial 200 mg phase lasted just 5 days.
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Bezlotoxumab is one infusion of 10 mg/kg over 60 minutes, given at some point while standard CDI antibiotics are still running;** its half-life is about 18 days, so antibody stays measurable for up to 3 months.
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Where access is not a problem, a first episode plus another recurrence risk factor (age 65 or over, immunocompromise, severe CDI at presentation) may also warrant bezlotoxumab;** evidence for it alongside fidaxomicin is limited.
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Benefit grows with the number of risk factors:** on placebo, 37.2% with any risk factor recurred against 20.9% with none, and a first episode with no risk factor gained nothing from bezlotoxumab.
claims.locator: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, Gonzales-Luna AJ, Garey KW, Kelly CP, Wilcox MH; IDSA and SHEA, Clinical Infectious Diseases 73(5):e1029 (doi 10.1093/cid/ciab549), 'Clinical Practice Guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 Focused Update Guidelines on Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Adults', published 14 June 2021, https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridioides-difficile-2021-focused-update/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **First non-severe recurrence, regimens compared (S1 Table 2):** IDSA/SHEA: standard or extended-pulsed fidaxomicin, tapered-and-pulsed vancomycin, or a standard vancomycin course, adding bezlotoxumab if the previous episode was within 6 months. ESCMID: standard fidaxomicin if it was not used for the first episode, or fidaxomicin or vancomycin with bezlotoxumab; tapered-and-pulsed vancomycin only when nothing else can be had. ASID 2016: vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours for 10 days.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second or later non-severe recurrence (S1 Table 2):** IDSA/SHEA: fidaxomicin (standard or extended-pulsed), tapered-and-pulsed vancomycin, or vancomycin for 10 days then rifaximin 400 mg every 8 hours for 20 days, plus bezlotoxumab if an episode occurred in the prior 6 months; offer FMT only after antibiotic treatment of at least two recurrences (three episodes). ESCMID: FMT after fidaxomicin or vancomycin pre-treatment, or either drug with bezlotoxumab. ASID 2016: vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours for 14 days with or without a taper, fidaxomicin, FMT if available, or vancomycin then rifaximin.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Schedules (S1 Table 2 notes):** extended-pulsed fidaxomicin is 200 mg every 12 hours for 5 days, then 200 mg every other day for 20 days. A sample tapered-and-pulsed vancomycin course: 125 mg four times a day for 10–14 days, twice a day for 7 days, once a day for 7 days, then every 2–3 days for a further 2–8 weeks. Adjunctive bezlotoxumab is 10 mg/kg IV once, during standard antibiotics.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tapered-and-pulsed oral vancomycin** is an acceptable alternative to fidaxomicin (standard or extended-pulsed) for a first or later recurrence.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FMT:** ESCMID and Australasian guidelines agree on it for a second recurrence; IDSA/SHEA now limits it to the third and later recurrences after donor-transmitted infection alerts. A single FMT cures 65%–95% by any route.
claims.locator: Bishop EJ, Tiruvoipati R (Peninsula Health and Monash University, Melbourne), Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 'Management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and challenges in clinical practice: review and comparison of current IDSA/SHEA, ESCMID and ASID guidelines', published 28 November 2022 (J Antimicrob Chemother 78(1):21), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9780550/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Probiotics are not endorsed** by current CDI guidelines; ESCMID warns of possibly significant adverse effects and delayed microbiome recovery, and there are reports of bacteraemia and fungaemia.

claims.claim: **Routine anti-CDI antibiotic prophylaxis during systemic antibiotics is not recommended (ESCMID)**; it may suit very selected patients with multiply recurrent CDI triggered by antibiotics, after specialist infectious diseases or microbiology advice.
